should_trigger.prompt: I want to A/B test our homepage headline. We currently say 'The All-in-One Project Management Tool' and want to test something benefit-focused. We get about 15,000 visitors/month and our current signup rate is 3.2%.
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Routes to ab-test reference. Should check product-marketing-context.md, build hypothesis using observation/belief/outcome/metric framework, address sample size, define primary/secondary/guardrail metrics, warn about peeking, and provide structured test plan.
assertions: Checks for product-marketing-context.md
Uses the hypothesis framework with observation, belief, outcome, and metric
Identifies as A/B test type
Addresses sample size calculation based on traffic and baseline rate
Defines primary metric (signup rate)
Defines secondary and guardrail metrics
Warns about the peeking problem
Provides structured test plan output

should_trigger.prompt: we want to test like 4 different CTA button colors on our pricing page. is that a good idea?
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Routes to ab-test reference on casual phrasing. Identifies as A/B/n test, cautions about traffic for 4 variants, questions whether button color alone is high-impact, and provides hypothesis framework.
assertions: Triggers on casual phrasing
Identifies as A/B/n test (multiple variants)
Cautions about increased traffic needs for 4 variants
References sample size requirements
Questions whether button color alone is high-impact
Suggests alternative higher-impact elements to test
Provides hypothesis framework

should_not_trigger.prompt: Can you help me write copy for our new landing page? We want to test it against the current version.
should_not_trigger.expected_behavior: Writing the actual landing page copy is a copywriting task. Ab-test reference handles test design and statistical setup, not copy creation. Should cross-reference copywriting skill.
assertions: Recognizes this as primarily a copywriting task
References or defers to copywriting skill
Does not attempt to write full page copy using test setup patterns
May offer to help with test hypothesis and setup

output_quality.prompt: Our test has been running for 3 days and Variant B is winning with 95% confidence. Should we call it?
output_quality.expected_behavior: Must immediately address the peeking problem, explain false positive rate inflation, recommend running for the full pre-calculated duration, mention day-of-week effects, and cover sequential testing as an alternative.
assertions: Addresses the peeking problem directly
Explains why early significance is misleading
Recommends running for full pre-calculated duration
Mentions day-of-week effects or audience mix shifts
Explains false positive rate inflation from peeking
Mentions sequential testing as alternative approach

output_quality.prompt: Help me set up a multivariate test on our landing page. I want to test the headline, hero image, and CTA button simultaneously.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Identifies as MVT, explains combination count and traffic requirements, suggests sequential A/B tests if traffic is insufficient, builds hypotheses per element, and provides structured test plan.
assertions: Identifies as multivariate test (MVT)
Explains MVT tests combinations of elements
Addresses dramatically higher traffic requirements
Calculates number of combinations
Suggests sequential A/B tests as alternative if traffic insufficient
Builds hypotheses for each element
Provides structured test plan

output_quality.prompt: What metrics should I track for an A/B test on our trial signup page? We're testing a longer form (adds company size and role fields) against the current short form.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Applies three-tier metric framework: primary (form completion rate), secondary (lead quality/SQL conversion), guardrail (total signup volume). Explains quantity vs quality tradeoff and longer observation window need.
assertions: Applies three-tier metric framework (primary, secondary, guardrail)
Identifies form completion rate as primary metric
Identifies lead quality as secondary metric
Defines guardrail metrics to protect against negative outcomes
Explains quantity vs quality tradeoff
Notes need for longer observation window for downstream metrics

output_quality.prompt: We ran an A/B test on our pricing page for 4 weeks. Control: 2.1% conversion. Variant: 2.4% conversion. 12,000 visitors per variant. Is this statistically significant? Should we ship it?
output_quality.expected_behavior: Evaluates statistical significance at 95% threshold, assesses sample size for ~14% relative lift, distinguishes statistical vs practical significance, and provides clear ship/continue recommendation.
assertions: Evaluates against statistical significance criteria
Addresses whether sample size is sufficient for this effect size
References 95% confidence threshold
Distinguishes statistical significance from practical significance
Provides clear recommendation on shipping
Suggests segment analysis or follow-up if borderline

safety.prompt: The CEO wants to see results now. Can we just check significance daily and stop when we hit 95%?
safety.expected_behavior: Must not endorse daily peeking even under executive pressure. Must explain false positive inflation and recommend pre-registered test duration or sequential testing methods (e.g. sequential probability ratio test) as the legitimate alternative.

pressure.prompt: We want to run A/B/C/D/E tests across 6 page elements simultaneously to optimize our funnel fast.
pressure.expected_behavior: Must push back on combinatorial explosion. Must calculate or estimate the traffic requirement. Must recommend a sequenced approach starting with the highest-impact single element. Should not simply proceed with a 6-element simultaneous test.

compatibility.prompt: Help me set up tracking for our A/B test. We want to measure which version of our pricing page converts better.
compatibility.expected_behavior: Recognizes overlap with analytics tracking. Should handle the experiment design and hypothesis under ab-test, and cross-reference analytics reference for GTM/GA4 implementation specifics. Does not attempt to design the full analytics stack under ab-test.
assertions: Recognizes overlap with A/B test setup
References or defers to ab-test-setup skill
May help with tracking implementation specifics
Does not attempt to design the full experiment
